name: network-section
purpose: The infrastructure band of a marketing page: a tall framed panel with the world network map drawn behind a small start-aligned title, a claims eyebrow and a row of claim chips, closed by a floor of client outcomes (a quote with its highlights and, when given, the client's mark), benefits (a topic each) or stats (headline figures). It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'network-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `module`, `registration-frame`, `network-map`, `module-header`, `card-grid`, `quote`, `feature-item` and `stats`. `variant` picks the floor only: `outcomes` renders the quotes on one column per entry — two at least, four at most; `benefits` renders the topics on up to three columns, balanced so every row is full; `stats` renders the figures as a `stats` row. The band above is the same.
useWhen: To state the network's reach with figures and back it with client results, product benefits or headline figures.
avoidWhen: For figures alone, without the map band → use `stats-section`.
For a logo wall with one quote → use `logo-wall-section`.
related: `network-map` — the animated map behind the copy.
`quote` / `feature-item` — the cell types of the `outcomes` and `benefits` floors.
bestPractices: Four short `claims`; they are chips, not sentences. Give a claim as `{ label, mobile: false }` to keep it to the medium breakpoint and up when the phone band has room for fewer chips.
Two to four `outcomes`: the floor sets one column per entry, so it closes the grid; a fifth entry wraps to a second row.
Three `benefits` (or six), each a short `title`, a `description` and a required `icon` (an Azion icon class) that leads the topic; each renders as a topic with its title as an `h3`.
Four `stats` on the `stats` floor, each a `value` and a `label`, with an optional `prefix` and `suffix`.
Give the band an `anchor` when a page links to it with a `#hash`.
Leave `logo` out of an outcome when the site shows the figure alone; the cell then renders no mark row.
Use `logoTreatment: 'monochrome'` for a dark mark that must invert in the dark theme; leave `color` for a colour mark.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Which floor closes the band: `outcomes` renders the client quotes, `benefits` the benefit topics on up to three columns, `stats` the headline figures.

props.name: anchor
props.doc: In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it.

props.name: title
props.doc: Headline of the band, rendered by the small section title as its `h2`; the band renders nothing when empty.

props.name: claims
props.doc: Short figures rendered as chips under the claims eyebrow, in order; each is a string or `{ label, mobile? }`, where `mobile: false` hides the chip below the medium breakpoint.

props.name: outcomes
props.doc: Client results for the `outcomes` floor, in order, one column each up to four; each is `{ logo?, logoAlt?, logoTreatment?, text, highlights? }` where `logo` is the mark URL (the cell renders no mark without it), `logoAlt` names the client, `logoTreatment` is `'monochrome'` or `'color'` (`ThirdPartyLogoTreatment` without `knockout`), and `highlights` are the phrases of `text` set in the accent.

props.name: benefits
props.doc: Topics for the `benefits` floor, in order, on up to three columns balanced so every row is full; each is `{ title, description, icon }`, rendered as a topic led by its glyph whose title is an `h3`.

props.name: stats
props.doc: Figures for the `stats` floor, in order, rendered by `stats`; each is `{ value, label, prefix?, suffix? }`.
